$X$ is normally distributed, $P(X<62)=0.5$ and $P(X<86)=0.9938$.

Use $P(Z<2)=0.9772$ and $P(Z<2.5)=0.9938$.

Took the mean from the score with probability $0.9938$ rather than the one with probability $0.5$.
Took the wrong score as the mean and also read $z=2$ instead of $z=2.5$.

questions.solution_text:
A probability of $0.5$ marks the mean, because the curve is symmetrical about it.
$\mu=62$
$0.9938$ is greater than $0.5$, so $86$ lies above the mean and $z$ is positive.
$z=2.5$
$2.5=\frac{86-62}{\sigma}$
$2.5\sigma=24$
$\sigma=9.6$

questions.question_text:
Batteries are produced at a factory.
The batteries are normally distributed with a mean of 28 hours and a standard deviation of $\sigma$.
Given that 5% of batteries fail, and that only batteries with a life less than 24.052 hours fail, find the value of $\sigma$.

options.why: Uses an inaccurate standard Normal percentile or subtraction.
Confuses the distance from the mean with the standard deviation.
Squares or otherwise misuses the standardised distance.

questions.solution_text: The fifth percentile has standardised value $z=-1.645$. Hence $\frac{24.052-28}{\sigma}=-1.645$. Thus $\sigma=\frac{3.948}{1.645}=2.4$ hours.
